During a practice session in a stadium an athlete runs along a circular track and her performance is observed by her coach standing at point on the circle and also by her physiotherapist standing at the centre of the circle. The coach finds that she covers an angle of 72° in 1 min. what will be the angle covered by her in 1 second according to the measurement made by her physiotherapist?

options.text: It depends on the position of the coach on the circular track

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6961176d393c8c0b9ba3a070ab5013bdd71fa57a9826d3a3b156eb03f1f51abc.png] 

Let the athlete runs from A to B in 1 minute and the coach and the physiotherapist observe him from point C and P respectively

Given, ∠ACB = 72°

The angle subtended by the arc at the centre is double of the angle subtended by the arc at a point on the circle.

⇒ ∠APB = 2 × 72 = 144°

Hence, according to physiotherapist the athlete covers an angle of 144° per minute

∴ In 1 second, the angle covered by the athlete according to physiotherapist = 144/60 = 2.4°

questions.question:
The full marks for a paper is 300. The break-up of the marks into theory (X), practical (Y) and project (Z), Which are the three components of evaluation is 6 : 5 : 4. In order to pass one has to score at least 40%, 50% and 50% respectively in X, Y, Z and 60% in aggregate. The marks scored by four students A, B, C and D are shown in the given Bar Graph.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59280376c8edf4c5f0228ce10a563e8b7c1b992b79f7af561f1fe0e219541acf.png] 

Arrange the students B, C and D according to the ascending order of the aggregate marks scored by them.
questions.solution:
The aggregate marks scored by B = (50 × 6/15) + (50 × 5/15) + (30 × 4/15) = 44.66

The aggregate marks scored by C = (70 × 6/15) + (80 × 5/15) + (60 × 4/15) = 70.66

The aggregate marks scored by D = (80 × 6/15) + (70 × 5/15) + (30 × 4/15) = 63.33

∴ The ascending order = B, D, C

questions.question: ΔABC ~ ΔDEF and their perimeters are 64 cm and 48 cm respectively. What is the length AB, if DE is equal to 9 cm?
questions.solution:
ΔABC ∼ ΔDEF

⇒ AB/DE = Perimeter of ΔABC/Perimeter of ΔDEF

⇒ AB/9 = 64/48

⇒ AB = 64/48 × 9

∴ AB = 12 cm

questions.question: A certain sum was invested on simple interest. The amount to which it had grown in five years was 1(1)/(4) times the amount to which it had grown in three years. The percentage rate of interest was:
questions.solution:
Let the amount invested be Rs. 100 and the rate of interest be x

Simple interest for 5 year = PRT/100 = (100 × x × 5)/100 = 5x

⇒ Amount at the end of 5 years = P + I = 100 + 5x

Simple interest for 3 years = PRT/100 = (100 × x × 3)/100 = 3x

Amount at the end of 3 years = P + I = 100 + 3x

According to question:

100 + 5x = 5/4(100 + 3x)

⇒ 400 + 20x = 500 + 15x

⇒ 5x = 100

⇒ x = 20%

questions.question: What is the value of cosec² 30° + sin² 45° + sec² 60° + tan² 30?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute the **standard trigonometric values**: cosec 30° = 2, sin 45° = 1/√2, sec 60° = 2, and tan 30° = 1/√3.

Expression = 2² + (1/√2)² + 2² + (1/√3)²

Expression = 4 + 1/2 + 4 + 1/3

Expression = 8 + (3 + 2) ÷ 6 = 8 + 5/6 = 53/6

**∴ The correct answer is 53/6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cosec² 30° + sin² 45° + sec² 60° + tan² 30°

**Formula Used:** Values of **Trigonometric Ratios** for specific angles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0e442760aefaedcece4bc9216ac7c7e6d2d64d34daf5f022eeccfa5ef6e7e7a.png] 

⇒ cosec 30° = 2

⇒ sin 45° = 1/√2

⇒ sec 60° = 2

⇒ tan 30° = 1/√3

⇒ Value = (2)² + (1/√2)² + (2)² + (1/√3)²

⇒ Value = 4 + 1/2 + 4 + 1/3

⇒ Value = 8 + (3 + 2) ÷ 6

⇒ Value = 8 + 5/6 = 53/6

Thus, the final calculated value corresponds to option (3).

**∴ The correct answer is 53/6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Table Values

Values for common angles: sin 30° = 1/2, sin 45° = 1/√2, cos 60° = 1/2, tan 30° = 1/√3, and cot 45° = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

cosec θ = 1 ÷ sin θ | sec θ = 1 ÷ cos θ | cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

Square Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.</p

questions.question: For 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, what is θ, when √3 cos θ + sin θ = 1?
questions.solution:
By hit and trial method:

Taking the value of θ = 90°

L.H.S.

√3 cosθ + sinθ

= √3 cos90° + sin90°

= √3 (0) + 1

= 1

= R.H.S.

∴ θ = 90°

questions.question: The average of 1088 real numbers is zero. At most how many of them can be negative?
questions.solution:
We know, Average of quantities = sum of all quantities/no. of quantities

The average of 1088 numbers is zero.

So, the summation of 1088 numbers = 1088 × 0 = 0

If the summation of 1087 numbers = - (1088th number) then only summation of 1088 number will be zero.

∴ Out of 1088 numbers, at most 1087 numbers may be greater than zero.

A can complete a piece of work in 20 days and B can complete 20% of the work in 6 days. If they work together in how many days can they finish 50% of the work, if they work together?
questions.solution:
A completes a piece of work in 20 days.

⇒ One day work of A = 1/20

B completes 20% of the work in 6 days.

⇒ B will complete 100% of the work in 6 × 100/20 = 30 days.

One day work of B = 1/30

When A and B work together, their one day work = 1/20 + 1/30

⇒ (3 + 2)/60

⇒ 5/60

⇒ 1/12

⇒ A and B working together can complete the whole work in 12 days.

∴ A and B together can complete 50% of the work in 12/2 = 6 days

questions.question: With reference to a number greater than one, the difference between itself and its reciprocal is 25% of the sum of itself and its reciprocal. By how much percentage (correct one decimal place) is the fourth power of the number greater than its square?
questions.solution:
Let the number be x.

According to the question:

X – 1/x = 25/100 × (x + 1/x)

⇒ x² – 1 = ¼ (x² + 1)

⇒ 4x² – 4 = x² + 1

⇒ 3x² = 5

⇒ x² = 5/3

⇒ x⁴ = 25/9

∴ Required percentage = frac{{( {frac{{25}}{9} - (5)/(3)} )}}{{(5)/(3)}} times 100 = 66.7\%

questions.question: AB and CD are two chords of a circle which intersect at a point O inside the circle. It is given that, AB = 10 cm, CO = 1.5 cm and DO = 12.5 cm. What is the ratio between the larger and smaller among AO and BO?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e60e161fe18d2aa130770be4be539d2eb0308aa4ef20f412217f3c3e95e38a0b.png] 

Let two chords AB and CD intersect inside the circle at the point O:

Hence **intersecting chords theorem** is used which means that the products of the lengths of the line segments on each chord are equal

AO × OB = CO × DO

⇒ x(10 – x) = 1.5 × 12.5

⇒ 10x – x² = 18.75

⇒ x² – 10x + 18.75 = 0

⇒ 100x² – 1000x + 1875 = 0

⇒ 4x² – 40x + 75 = 0

⇒ 4x² – 30x – 10x + 75 = 0

⇒ 2x(2x – 15) – 5(2x – 15) = 0

⇒ (2x – 5)(2x – 15) = 0

⇒ x = 5/2 or x = 15/2

When x = 5/2,

(10 – x) = (10 – 5/2) = 15/2

When x = 15/2,

(10 – x) = (10 – 15/2) = 5/2

∴ The ratio of the larger and smaller among AO and BO = 15/2: 5/2 = 3: 1

questions.question: The two diagonals of a rhombus are respectively, 14 cm and 48 cm. The perimeter of the rhombus is equal to:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38d57be7996457ee0dbbcd103961234b329975b999ba6f16ccc788e6507860e3.png] 

In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at right angle

Let the diagonal AC = 14 cm and BD = 48 cm

⇒ AO = 14/2 = 7 cm and BO = 48/2 = 24 cm

In ΔAOB, AB² = AO² + BO²

⇒ AB² = 7² + 24²

⇒ AB² = 49 + 576

⇒ AB² = 625

⇒ AB = 25 cm

∴ Perimeter of the rhombus = 4 × side of rhombus = 4 × 25 = 100 cm

questions.question: The platform of a station 400 m long starts exactly where the last span of a bridge 1.2 km long ends. How long will a train 200 m long and travelling at the speed of 72 km/h take to cover the distance between the starting point of the span of the bride and the far end of the platform?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total distance = **Length of Bridge** + **Length of Platform** + **Length of Train**

Total distance = 1200 m + 400 m + 200 m = 1800 m

Speed = 72 km/h = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

Time = 1800 / 20 = 90 seconds = 1.5 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/732b7e15ae176a3c9e9539afbd3e1c3e90c8c46412e60227df6b903d26ca6075.png] 

**Given:**

Length of **Bridge** = 1.2 km = 1200 m

Length of **Platform** = 400 m

Length of **Train** = 200 m

**Speed of Train** = 72 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 1200 + 400 + 200 = 1800 m

⇒ Speed in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s

⇒ Time (in sec) = 1800 ÷ 20 = 90 seconds

⇒ Time (in min) = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 min

**∴ The correct answer is 1.5 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Total Distance for Crossing

When a train crosses a stationary object of length L, the total distance covered is Length of Train + L.

Average Speed

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy / (x+y).</p
